exposure_disclosure:
Heavy and disqualifying for independence purposes; stated in full because a thin disclosure would make this record worthless.

(1) Before opening a single byte of the object I had read the repository's own port of it at governance/protocols/OP-PROT-019-v1.1_R17.md, in full. That port is a derived copy of this very object (see finding OBJ-01), so I came to the exact bytes already knowing the document's whole argument, section by section.

(2) I had read docs/R17_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md, the author-side installation report, which states the conclusions I was asked to test: that thirteen adversarial test groups passed under normal and optimized Python, that R17 'replaces the proposed guarantees with precise behavior', and that 'Sheets coordination remains cooperative rather than race-free'. I had therefore seen the author's own summary of the result before reconstructing anything, which is exactly the access OP-PROT-012 §5(c) forbids to an independent-eyes reviewer.

(3) I had read governance/GIT_ADAPTATION.md, including the publication-race row I was separately asked to challenge, and OP-PROT-012 in full.

(4) I had read the README, docs/RESEARCH_MAP.md section headings and docs/OPEN_PROBLEMS.md sections D, E and F, so I knew before starting that this route is one of 24, that it is one of only three at technical status READY (RV-RN3, RV-P15, RV-OPS-R17), that docs/OPEN_PROBLEMS.md §D describes all 24 as unassigned — a claim I later found to be off by one, see finding OBJ-13, and that section F already reports three Quarantine Index rows using an EXISTING_CONTAINER class that OP-PROT-019 §6 does not define. That last item is a pre-existing repository finding, not mine; my Case 4 probe rediscovered the same gap from the implementation side, and I have labelled it as corroboration rather than as a new finding.

(5) I had read reviews/README.md and reviews/SCHEMA.md, which quote R17 §4 verbatim and argue five places where the protocol and the contribution plan's summary differ. Those quotations primed me on §4's wording before I read §4 in the object.

(6) Lineage exposure, the most serious item. This session belongs to the same Anthropic lineage that produced this repository's port of the object, the ported implementation report, GIT_ADAPTATION.md, OPEN_PROBLEMS.md and the review-record schema I am writing into. I am not a coauthor of the Drive object, whose author lineage is OpenAI, but I am downstream of an Anthropic re-expression of it and I reused that re-expression as my entry point.

(7) What I had NOT seen before this review, and what therefore carries more weight: r17_reference.py, test_r17_reference.py, TESTS_NORMAL.txt, TESTS_OPTIMIZED.txt and 00_HANDOFF_SUMMARY_OPS4.json. None of those five is reproduced anywhere in this repository; I obtained and digest-verified all five during this review and had no prior sight of any of them.

(8) Bias direction. Reading the author's favourable report first biases toward agreement, and I did in fact confirm its headline claim. The counterweight I applied is that every adverse finding below was produced by executing something, not by reading, and each is reproducible from the commands in the Markdown companion.
hypotheses: Operator authorization is not evidence: 'Dylan Roy directly authorized this overhaul... This authorization is not a proof, an independence credit, or approval of an unresolved theorem.' Every rule below inherits that disclaimer.

Concurrency is cooperative, not transactional: 'Sheets batch updates are atomic within one request, **not a compare-and-swap lock across clients**... This is cooperative coordination, not a hard distributed mutex.'

No hard lock is installed: 'If a strict machine-enforced lock is required, a transaction-capable service is still needed; none is represented as installed here.'

The decisive scope hypothesis on the accompanying code: 'The accompanying local reference validator and adversarial tests demonstrate protocol predicates on specified inputs. They are not a deployed enforcement service and do not prove race freedom for Google Drive.' Every claim about the bundled code is conditional on 'on specified inputs'.
reconstruction:
The object is an operational policy in eight sections, not a mathematical argument, so 'reconstructing the argument' means restating each normative rule in my own terms and then executing the accompanying predicates against adversarial inputs rather than reading along with the author's tests.

§1 makes one entry point normative and demotes predecessor protocols to reference history. §2 replaces a mandatory whole-Drive preflight with a bounded cached entry, and makes identity digest-based: reuse bytes only by exact digest plus extraction rule, treat modifiedTime as non-probative, and revalidate before publishing. The handoff is an immutable {payload, payload_sha256} envelope over a deterministic restricted JSON encoding, with no self-referential hash field, and a stale handoff triggers bounded revalidation rather than a crawl. §3 makes coordination an append-only Work Events log: order contenders by confirmed append position rather than self-reported timestamp, 120-minute leases renewed by heartbeats naming the same claim and session, and publication guarded by recheck-then-publish with two successors of one head held as a conflict for explicit reconciliation. §4 separates four dimensions and permits a fresh nonauthor session of any provider, including the author's, to do technical review at zero organizational independence. §5 separates request time from last substantive activity and makes 7/14/30-day aging a pickup ladder that never approves. §6 gives five quarantine classifications with an evidence column and a logical-quarantine mechanism for frozen archive members, keyed by carrier ID plus relative path and hash, restorable only by a new erratum or successor plus a fresh review. §7 is the DRAFT to CANDIDATE_VERIFIED to READY_FOR_REVIEW to REVIEWED/AMEND ladder, in which registration is custody rather than review completion. §8 evaluates v1.0's four proposals and rejects three of them as stated.

The object's load-bearing self-claim is its last line: an accompanying local reference validator and adversarial tests 'demonstrate protocol predicates on specified inputs'. I resolved that claim to two archive members of R17_NAVIGATION_REVIEW_AND_ROLLBACK.zip, obtained both, verified them against their recorded member digests, and read them. r17_reference.py implements nine predicates: instant, canonical, digest, envelope, handoff_status, winner, publication_conflicts, review_class and quarantine_class. I re-derived each against the section it claims to implement.

handoff_status is a guard chain: envelope shape exactly {payload, payload_sha256}; recomputed payload digest; required field set present and non-empty; per-source drive_id/sha256/bytes/extraction present, with a 64-lowercase-hex digest and a non-negative int byte count; no future checkpoint; then equality against live protocol_version, target_key, task_id, sources, output_head and claim_id plus claim_valid; and only then age, returning SCOPED_REVALIDATION above 7200 seconds and FAST_ROUTE_VALID below. Putting age last is the right order and I confirmed it: a stale handoff whose head also moved reports HEAD_CHANGED, not staleness.

winner projects the ledger. It canonicalises each event, treats a byte-identical repeat of an ID as idempotent and a conflicting reuse as an error, rejects any event dated after the supplied clock, requires a lease strictly after its event and at most 120 minutes long, requires a heartbeat to name its own claim and session, to arrive before expiry, and to come from the current minimum-row eligible claim, and finally returns the eligible claim with the smallest append row. That is §3's 'earliest append position controls primary publication' implemented literally.

publication_conflicts groups PUBLISH events by (target, old_head) and reports any group with more than one distinct new_head. review_class gates on disclosure and substantiveness, routes authors and flagged coauthors to INTERNAL_VERIFICATION with org_independent False, and otherwise returns NONAUTHOR_TECHNICAL_REVIEW with org_independent set by provider-set membership. quarantine_class is a four-branch classifier: defect, then superseded, then byte equality, then UNVERIFIED.

Rather than take the author's receipts on trust I ran the bundled suite myself: 13 groups, all passing, under both plain python3 and python3 -OO. I then verified the author's shipped handoff end to end: 00_HANDOFF_SUMMARY_OPS4.json recomputes to its own recorded payload_sha256 41e6b541cd1e5c7b216a3859d18745dafcd22d391da6d9602d1fd1d44d9c21bc under the object's own canonical encoder, its file digest matches the archive member index, and its single declared source is this object by ID, digest and byte count. Evaluated against a matching live state it returns FAST_ROUTE_VALID at the checkpoint hour and SCOPED_REVALIDATION a day later, which is the §2 behaviour as written.

findings.criterion: identity / port fidelity of the repository copy
findings.statement: This repository's governance/protocols/OP-PROT-019-v1.1_R17.md is NOT the reviewed object. It is a whitespace-normalised derivative whose byte count coincidentally equals the object's, so a byte-count check confirms the wrong bytes. Anyone who reviews 'the protocol' from the repository path is not reviewing the object the register names.
findings.evidence: Object: 14,073 bytes / 04987ba4…7390. Repository copy: 14,073 bytes / efcfdd5cde32e7bd706f432689f5b022b0a2a8ec289164eed170a61d7a0071d9. `diff` reduces the difference to two whitespace edits — a blank line inserted after line 1, and one trailing newline removed at line 91 — which cancel in length; `cmp -l` reports 13,724 differing byte positions from the resulting one-byte shift. R17 §2 is explicit that identity is the exact digest; §6 EXACT_DUPLICATE requires 'matching raw digest/bytes'. This copy matches neither.

findings.criterion: §6 restoration — the fourth case named in the review brief
findings.statement: Restoration is not implemented and not tested. R17 §6 gives a logical-quarantine mechanism keyed by carrier ID plus relative path and hash, restorable by 'a new erratum/successor and fresh review'. The reference module exposes nine callables and not one of them accepts an erratum, a successor, a fresh review, a move record or a carrier-plus-path-plus-hash exclusion key. The single bundled quarantine test exercises classification only.
findings.evidence: Public surface of r17_reference.py: canonical, digest, envelope, handoff_status, instant, publication_conflicts, quarantine_class, review_class, winner. Enumerating quarantine_class over every argument combination yields exactly four outputs — DEFECTIVE_SCOPE, EXACT_DUPLICATE, SUPERSEDED, UNVERIFIED — so the fifth §6 classification LEGACY_INSPIRATION is unreachable and 'UNVERIFIED / CONFLICT' collapses to UNVERIFIED with no way to distinguish the two. Corroborates, from the implementation side, the pre-existing repository finding in docs/OPEN_PROBLEMS.md §F that three live Quarantine Index rows use an EXISTING_CONTAINER class §6 does not define.

findings.criterion: §4 independence — vacuous credit against an unestablished author lineage
findings.statement: review_class awards organizational independence VACUOUSLY when the author lineage is unknown, because independence is computed as set non-membership against a possibly empty provider list. Eleven of the 24 Review Queue rows are in exactly that state: RV-DQ-005, -017, -020, -023, -027, -035, -038, -053, -057, -061 and -096 each carry 'Disclose exact-object authorship; provider alone is insufficient' in the Author/provider column, and thirteen rows carry an unresolved Body SHA-256.
findings.evidence: review_class([], [], 'fresh', 'Anthropic', True, True) returns {'technical': 'NONAUTHOR_TECHNICAL_REVIEW', 'org_independent': True}. The author's own suite tests the empty-author case only with substantive=False, where the disclosure gate short-circuits to CANNOT_VERIFY, so the vacuous branch is never reached by a bundled test. Note that this repository's own tools/reviews_check.py is stricter than the protocol's reference implementation here: it refuses any nonzero credit when author_family is 'unknown'. Counts re-derived from registers/json/review_queue.json during this review, after an earlier draft of this record misstated them as four; the corrected figures are 11 unresolved-authorship rows of 24 and 3 rows at technical status READY.

findings.criterion: §4 independence — the second-credit and reused-reasoning rules are unimplemented
findings.statement: Two explicit §4 sentences have no representation in the reference implementation. 'Existing independent verdicts retain their exact scope; do not award a second credit to the same lineage' — review_class takes no prior-credit or lineage argument, so two successive reviewers of one provider each receive org_independent True. 'Different provider alone does not establish independence if it coauthored the target or reused the same reasoning' — only coauthorship has a parameter; reused reasoning has none.
findings.evidence: review_class(['auth'], ['OpenAI'], 'anthropic-session-1', 'Anthropic', True, True) and the same call with 'anthropic-session-2' both return org_independent True. A different-provider reviewer replaying the author's own derivation is indistinguishable from a genuinely separate one.

findings.criterion: §4 independence — provider identity is an exact case-sensitive string
findings.statement: Provider matching is raw string membership, so any spelling drift silently converts zero independence into one. With author provider ['OpenAI'], a reviewer declaring 'openai', 'OPENAI', 'OpenAI ' or 'Open AI' is each reported as organizationally independent.
findings.evidence: Four of five spellings tested return org_independent True; only the byte-identical 'OpenAI' returns False. No normalisation, canonical provider vocabulary or validation exists, and no bundled test varies the spelling.

findings.criterion: §2 stale handoff — the 120-minute boundary sits inside the fast route
findings.statement: §2 says 'A 120-minute-old handoff triggers bounded revalidation'. The implementation uses a strict dt>7200, so a handoff of exactly 120 minutes returns FAST_ROUTE_VALID and does not trigger revalidation. The boundary is off by one second relative to the sentence, in the permissive direction, and negative controls C1 and C3 show the bundled suite pins neither the constant nor the inequality.
findings.evidence: Ages 0, 119 and 120 minutes all return FAST_ROUTE_VALID; 121 minutes returns SCOPED_REVALIDATION. Severity is MINOR because the guard chain that actually protects correctness — policy, target, task, sources, head and claim equality — runs before the age test and is unaffected.

findings.criterion: §2 source identity — an empty extraction rule is accepted
findings.statement: §2 lists extraction rule among the required source identities and warns that native Docs need revision-aware extraction. handoff_status checks that the key is present, never that it says anything, so a source declaring extraction '' passes as a valid identity.
findings.evidence: A payload whose single source is {'drive_id': 'd', 'sha256': 'a'*64, 'bytes': 3, 'extraction': ''} returns FAST_ROUTE_VALID. By contrast an uppercase digest, a bool byte count and a negative byte count are all correctly rejected as BAD_SOURCE_IDENTITY, so the strictness is present elsewhere and simply absent here.

findings.criterion: §3 publication race — fork detection keyed on a self-reported field
findings.statement: publication_conflicts groups by the publisher's SELF-REPORTED old_head, which is precisely the field a racing or stale writer gets wrong. A genuine fork in which the second writer records the wrong predecessor is reported as no conflict at all. §3 elsewhere insists on 'the confirmed append position, not a self-reported timestamp'; the same distrust is not applied to old_head.
findings.evidence: Two successors of head h0 are correctly reported as {('X','h0'): ['a','b']}; changing only the second event's old_head to an incorrect value yields {} — the fork disappears. Additionally there is no RECONCILE event type and no predicate that a detected fork was ever resolved: a fork plus a reconciliation event is reported identically to the unreconciled fork.

findings.criterion: §3 publication race — no binding between claim and publication
findings.statement: §3 requires rechecking 'source/head/claim' immediately before moving a pointer, but no predicate joins winner() to PUBLISH events. A PUBLISH from a session holding no claim, or an expired one, is never flagged by anything in the module.
findings.evidence: With a valid claim held by session s1 (winner() returns 'C1'), a lone PUBLISH event from session s9 returns {} from publication_conflicts, and winner() is unaffected because it ignores PUBLISH events entirely. The two projections never meet.

findings.criterion: extraction channel — accessibility reading copies do not preserve blank-line runs
findings.statement: The sealed archive members are reachable only through derived reading-copy volumes, and that rendering is lossy: runs of blank lines are not preserved. Exact member bytes were recoverable only by testing candidate normalisations against a digest already known from the source map. For any object whose digest is not known in advance, this channel cannot establish exact bytes — which is the precondition R17 §2 makes identity depend on.
findings.evidence: Under one normalisation rule (strip trailing blanks, append two newlines) r17_reference.py and test_r17_reference.py reproduced exactly; the same rule gave 1,373 bytes for TESTS_NORMAL.txt against a recorded 1,370, and only collapsing blank-line runs and appending one newline produced the recorded digest. Three different candidate rules were needed across three members of one carrier.

findings.criterion: evidence receipts — the two bundled test receipts do not record their own invocation
findings.statement: The implementation report claims the suite passed 'under both normal Python and optimized Python'. The claim is true — I verified it — but the two shipped receipts cannot evidence it. They are 1,370 bytes each and differ in exactly one character of the elapsed-time line; neither records the interpreter, its version or its flags, and my own run under plain unoptimised python3 reproduced TESTS_OPTIMIZED.txt byte for byte.
findings.evidence: My verbose run: 1,370 bytes, sha256 bf59fa4f75a60c9cf2563f0517db0a8dda9b6e1e30af18e54627130be8c5fe5c, identical to the archive's TESTS_OPTIMIZED.txt. Diff against TESTS_NORMAL.txt: one line, 'Ran 13 tests in 0.003s' versus 'in 0.008s'. A receipt that omits its own command line cannot distinguish the two runs it is meant to distinguish.

findings.statement: Four of fifteen negative controls survived the bundled suite: the 120-minute staleness constant, the strict-versus-inclusive boundary at that constant, the zero-age future-checkpoint boundary, and the 120-minute maximum lease. The suite is genuinely adversarial on structure — shapes, guards, orderings, coauthorship — and weak on the two numeric constants §2 and §3 actually state.
findings.evidence: 11 of 15 mutants fired, each at the test group one would predict. C1 (7200 to 3600) survived while C2 (7200 to 1800) fired, bracketing the suite's sensitivity to the interval (3600, 10801] seconds. C5 (lease cap 120 to 240 minutes) survived because no fixture uses a lease longer than 120 minutes.

findings.criterion: quarantine_class — a present but empty defect is treated as no defect
findings.statement: The classifier branches on truthiness, so a recorded-but-empty defect field silently downgrades a DEFECTIVE_SCOPE case to EXACT_DUPLICATE. §6 requires a 'concrete failed statement, counterexample or reproducible invalid certificate chain' as evidence, which is a content requirement the implementation does not make.

findings.criterion: governance/GIT_ADAPTATION.md — the publication-race claim is overstated
findings.statement: GIT_ADAPTATION.md asserts 'Git gives the transactional guarantee the protocol says Sheets cannot: a push that races is rejected, never silently overwritten', and that a publication conflict becomes a merge conflict with 'Same semantics, machine-enforced'. The narrow kernel is true — a non-fast-forward update of one ref is an atomic compare-and-swap and is rejected — but three qualifications defeat the claim as written, and the row is internally inconsistent with the row above it. This is a finding about a repository document, not about the reviewed object, which claims nothing about git.
findings.evidence: (i) The same table prescribes 'A branch per claim; the PR is the claim'. Under branch-per-claim, two contenders push DIFFERENT refs, so nothing races and nothing is rejected: the fork R17 §3 describes is created without any git objection. (ii) The rejection is defeasible by --force, --force-with-lease, or delete-and-recreate. GIT_ADAPTATION itself says branch protection 'should' forbid force-push on main; in this repository receive.denyNonFastForwards and receive.denyDeletes are unset and no branch-protection configuration is present, so the guarantee is aspirational here rather than installed. (iii) 'Same semantics, machine-enforced' does not hold: `git merge-file` on two successors of one head editing disjoint regions of a proof body returns exit 0 and emits a third body neither claimant published, with no conflict raised — silent combination rather than the hold-and-reconcile §3 requires. The overlapping-edit case does return exit 1. Recommend restating the row as: git strengthens the same-ref case and leaves the cross-ref and auto-merge cases exactly as cooperative as the protocol says they are.

findings.criterion: self-description of the object — accurate, not overstated

scope_dependency_verdict:
Scope: this verdict covers the 14,073 bytes of OP-PROT-019-v1.1_R17.md at digest 04987ba4…7390 and, because the route names the *implementation*, the two accompanying code members I byte-verified — r17_reference.py and test_r17_reference.py — together with the TESTS_NORMAL.txt receipt and the OPS4 handoff envelope. It covers nothing else in the release folder and no live Drive surface.

Dependency verdict: the object's declared dependencies hold as far as I checked them. Its cited validator and adversarial tests exist, are byte-identifiable against the source map, and pass; its shipped handoff satisfies its own noncircular digest rule; its stated non-guarantees are consistent with what the code does. The AMEND is not a correctness failure of the document's statements. It is that three protocol rules the object itself states have no implementation in the bundle the object points at — §6 restoration of eligibility, §4's prohibition on a second credit to one lineage, and §4's reused-reasoning qualifier — and that two shipped predicates admit adversarial inputs they should reject: fork detection keyed on a self-reported old_head, and independence awarded vacuously against an empty author-provider list. Amendment means extending the reference implementation and its tests to those cases, or narrowing the object's final paragraph to name which predicates the bundle demonstrates and which it does not.

Scope firewall: nothing in this review touches the q0 2D upper track, the 3D lifetime track, or any relation between them, and nothing here is composed across them. This is an OPS-domain object; it has no mathematical content and carries no mathematical consequence in either direction.
independence_reason:
Zero, and the reason is not the usual one for this directory, so it is worth stating precisely. The author family is openai (Review Queue column 'OpenAI / OPS4-20260917-b9c2', corroborated by the OPS4 handoff payload); my family is anthropic. R17 §4's same-provider rule therefore does NOT apply here, and this is not a case where the credit is zero because reviewer and author share a lineage.

The credit is zero because the predicate that would license a nonzero one is not met. R17 §4: 'Different provider alone does not establish independence if it coauthored the target or reused the same reasoning.' OP-PROT-012 §5 lists the ten items (a)-(j) an independent-eyes credit requires, and at least four fail outright: (b) no frozen task specification existed before execution; (c) I had full access to the author's own implementation report and to this repository's derived port of the object before any freeze of my own, which is exactly the access (c) forbids; (e) no source or result hash was frozen before comparison — I compared as I went; (i) evidence-lineage disclosure reveals that this session is downstream of an Anthropic re-expression of the object, so OP-PROT-012 §5's closing rule, that shared hidden assumptions and repeated outputs count as one lineage, applies against me. I record the credit the predicate actually licenses, which is zero, and no more.

Separately and independently of all of the above: the external-independence predicate on this route REMAINS OPEN. The Review Queue row's Independence status reads EXTERNAL_REVIEW_OPEN and is exactly as open after this record as before it. An AMEND, or any other technical verdict, bears on the object and not on that predicate. R17 §4: 'A task may finish its technical review while an external-independence predicate remains open.'
does_not_establish:
1. No gate moves. No claim, premise, obligation or register row is promoted, closed, reclassified or otherwise moved from OPEN by this record. I edited no register; registers/, drive/ and claims/graph.json were read-only throughout. The RV-OPS-R17 row still reads Technical status READY, Independence status EXTERNAL_REVIEW_OPEN, Reviewer UNASSIGNED. This record does not change those cells and is not a request to.

2. No independence is created. The author lineage here is OpenAI and mine is Anthropic, which is a different family — and that fact still licenses zero credit, for the OP-PROT-012 §5 reasons set out in independence_reason. Nobody may cite this record as partial progress toward the external-review obligation, and an AMEND verdict is not a weaker form of an independent verdict; the two are different dimensions.

3. The AMEND is not a finding that the object is wrong. Every statement the object makes about itself that I could check held. AMEND records that specific protocol rules the object states lack implementation in the bundle it points at, and that two shipped predicates admit adversarial inputs. Do not read it as a defect in the policy's reasoning, and do not read the favourable half of this review as authority to invoke R17 for anything. Reviewing the governance machinery well is not permission to use it.

4. Passing the bundled suite establishes nothing about Google Drive. The suite exercises pure local functions on constructed inputs. It contains no Drive call, no Sheets call, no concurrency and no clock. §3's cooperative-coordination disclaimer is therefore untested here in the only setting that would matter, and my negative controls show the suite does not even pin the two numeric constants §2 and §3 state.

5. The four cases in the brief were answered only in the reference implementation's terms. Whether the deployed Drive workflow behaves as the reference does is outside what I can see; I never observed a real handoff being revalidated, a real lease contending, a real publication racing or a real quarantined member being restored.

6. My byte verification proves which bytes exist, not that the deployed system uses them. I confirmed the object's digest and three member digests. Nothing I did confirms that any live worker has ever loaded r17_reference.py, or that the two receipts were produced by the runs their filenames name — finding OBJ-09 shows they cannot evidence that.

7. Unverified dependencies remain unverified. Both carrier archives, the final custody receipt, the move log, the automation receipt, every quantitative figure in the implementation report, the live register surfaces and the three sibling protocols are listed in unresolved_dependencies and none of them is settled by this record.

8. Nothing mathematical is touched. No q0, SIDE24, RN, H5, LPW or prize-track object is reviewed, supported or weakened here; the 2D upper and 3D lifetime tracks are not composed anywhere in this work; and the count of original prize problems solved is unchanged at zero.

9. Age is not approval. This route is 1 day old at NEW, and neither its age nor the existence of this record makes it eligible for anything. R17 §5: 'Never turn age into automatic approval, invalidation, or extra independence.'
